author: For The Johnstonian News
title: Johnston County Public Library to offer fraud prevention, cybersecurity classes - NewsBreak
text:
By For The Johnstonian News ,
1 days ago
SMITHFIELD — The Public Library of Johnston County and Smithfield will offer free classes in October to help adults recognize fraud, protect personal information and practice safer online habits.
Detective Godwin of the Johnston County Sheriff’s Office will lead “Necessary Evils — How Not to Become a Victim of Fraud” from 1 to 2 p.m. Wednesday, Oct. 21, in the Multipurpose Meeting Room on the second floor of the Public Library of Johnston County and Smithfield.
The class will cover how scammers operate and provide practical ways to avoid becoming a victim of fraud. Registration is not required.
The library also will offer Cybersecurity Basics on Oct. 7, 14 and 28. The class will cover ways to use the internet safely, including protecting personal identities, personal data and financial assets while online.
Pre-registration is required.
To register for a Cybersecurity Basics Class or ask questions about either program, contact Stephanie at shaumont@pljcs.org or call 984-985-2665, ext. 8. The library is located at 305 E. Market St., Smithfield.
